subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should explicit continuation markers become shared core behavior, an optional plugin policy built on a generic inbound aggregation hook, or remain unsupported in favor of renewable debounce?
rationale: The choice adds public configuration and changes how separate inbound events become model-visible session turns; current code and related issues do not establish the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Generic plugin hook
options.body: Expose typed pre-agent aggregation and let an optional plugin own marker syntax, timeout, buffering, and release policy.

options.title: Shared core marker mode
options.body: Add one cross-channel marker contract with canonical configuration and complete flush, recovery, command, media, and typing semantics.

options.title: Keep debounce only
options.body: Treat renewable idle-time debounce as the supported cost-saving workflow and decline explicit marker-controlled completion.

recommendation.title: Generic plugin hook
recommendation.body: Expose typed pre-agent aggregation and let an optional plugin own marker syntax, timeout, buffering, and release policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current and historical ownership signal is on the shared inbound debounce and message-configuration boundary where this product contract would be defined.
